items.question: In your own words: what is Libre AI? What kind of organization is it and what makes its way of working unusual?

expectedElements.description: An independent open-source software lab building a product line/portfolio, not a single product.
The portfolio is built by AI agents operating under a governed method (Polaris) with human control gates.
Sovereignty/explainability commitments: open code, data under user control, traceable decisions, reversibility.
Honest status: nothing is released yet; foundations are being rebuilt from a clean base.

items.question: Where would you look for this project's published evidence (gates passed, verdicts, reports)? Name the concrete locations you can find.

expectedElements.description: The central repository libre-ai/libre-ai is where all current work and its record live.
The public evidence trail lives in distribution/evidence/ (gate acceptance log, reports, commitment hashes).
The forge documents itself: every pull request, decision and gate passed is visible in the repository.

items.question: The project states that nothing goes in the shop window that cannot be verified. Concretely, how would YOU verify one of its claims yourself, using only what is public?

expectedElements.description: Check the machine-readable inventory ecosystem/repositories.v1.yaml against the observable GitHub organization.
Trace a claim to its published record: the invariants register, ADRs, or a dated evidence report.
Every merge carries a DCO sign-off and green required checks — the CI gates are the enforcement.

items.question: You want to contribute a change or act on this project. What does it require from you, and where does the work actually happen?

expectedElements.description: Issues and pull requests for every product happen in the central repository libre-ai/libre-ai.
Every commit must carry a DCO sign-off.
CONTRIBUTING.md (with SECURITY.md) documents the contribution flow.
